Thanks for the details and the screenshots — reproduced locally. Summary and next steps below.

Root cause (short): The accept endpoint relies on a short-lived token in the query string but our frontend also reads a top-level session cookie to determine whether the user is an existing federated identity. In AlderTech's case their browser retained an older IdP session (guest feed) so the UI presented the org chooser instead of the accept flow. Two additional factors made it worse:
- The invite accept flow uses a cross-site navigation where SameSite=Lax is preventing the cookie from being excluded in some browsers, producing an ambiguous identity state.
- If the guest identity shares an email prefix but different domain aliasing (e.g., olivia.p@aldertech.com vs olivia.park@aldertech.com), our identity resolution prefers the existing session.

Immediate workarounds (use in order):
1) Incognito / Private Browser: clears the IdP session and allows the accept token to be consumed normally.
2) Direct accept URL: I'll issue a one-time accept link that includes a token and instructs the UI to ignore existing session cookies (link expires in 24 hours).
3) Manual provisioning: if they need PO access immediately, we can create the supplier record internally and mark it as invited; Ben, please confirm if you'd like me to do that for PO 78321.

Longer-term fix: engineering will update the accept flow to explicitly prioritize the accept-token when present (force accept regardless of session), and add a small client-side check to detect email alias collisions and surface a clearer "use another email" option. I will open a follow-up engineering task and link to support ticket 678432.

Action items for this thread:
- Rafael: create one-time direct accept URL and send to Olivia (doing now).
- Chloe: confirm whether AlderTech wants manual provisioning for PO 78321 if they can't accept within 24 hours.
- Ben: confirm billing/ops impact if manual provisioning is required.

Running note: created internal ticket ENG-11247 to track the accept-priority change.
